purpose: Reusable implementation context for HC-105 client-side real chat send/receive integration.
Helps future agents avoid re-discovery of the reducer gap, transport seam, and validation boundaries.
non_goals: Changing startup auth ownership or handshake behavior from HC-103.
Adding direct-message backend protocol or delivery semantics.
Expanding scope into room membership, persistence, or presence state.

tech_stack.name: Odin
tech_stack.usage_context: Primary language for client state, transport, and tests.

tech_stack.name: shared:skald
tech_stack.usage_context: UI and reducer event framework for chat input, state updates, and rendering.

tech_stack.name: ENet
tech_stack.usage_context: Established client/server transport that must gain explicit steady-state chat ownership after auth.

tech_stack.name: CBOR packet protocol
tech_stack.usage_context: Encodes shared room-chat payload structs and encrypted outer packets.

conventions: Use tabs, OTBS braces, and descriptive camelCase names with ID, URL, API, and HTTP uppercase conventions.
Client validation commands from client/AGENTS.md are odin check client, odin test client, odin build client, and odin run client.
Prefer additive changes over architectural rewrite; HC-105 is a focused client/runtime slice.
Prefer existing encrypted transport helpers and existing rich-text span rendering over new abstractions.

hard: Real server-backed room chat is the source of truth for visible room history.
HC-105 must now treat steady-state ENet poll and dispatch ownership as a first-class implementation slice.
Inbound room-chat events must carry enough metadata for selected-server, room, and self-versus-other behavior.
DM send is unsupported in HC-105 and must stop faking success.
Startup auth lifecycle remains owned by client/main.odin.
Validation stays narrow: client-focused Odin checks and tests.
soft: Keep implementation centered on client/main.odin, client/transport.odin, client/update.odin, client/view.odin, and client/main_test.odin unless a minimal protocol touch is required.
Reuse an existing error surface for failed send if possible before adding a new narrow chat-specific status field.
Preserve the current UI layout and focus only on behavioral correctness.
compatibility: HC-104 already handles ClientChatMessage on the server and emits ServerChatMessage for shared-room chat.
client/transport.odin already opens EncryptedPacket payloads after auth success and can seal encrypted packets through ClientServerTransport_buildEncryptedPacketBytes.
client/main.odin already tracks the selected server transport via selected_transport_index and owns startup auth via State_attemptSelectedServerStartup.
security_requirements: Only established authenticated transports may send or receive room-chat packets.
Do not bypass existing transport-state encryption helpers for app-level packets.
Protocol errors or failed sends must be surfaced narrowly without looking like delivered chat.

patterns: client/view.odin emits reducer messages only; direct network side effects do not originate in UI callbacks.
client/update.odin currently performs local fake send and uses placeholder receive handling, so reducer semantics are not yet authoritative.
client/main.odin is the lifecycle owner for selected-server startup auth and is the likeliest steady-state runtime owner candidate.
client/transport.odin has generic encrypted packet build/open primitives but no explicit post-auth room-chat poll or dispatch owner.

purpose: Shared room-chat payload contract already supported by HC-104.
why_relevant: HC-105 should reuse the existing room-chat payloads and avoid protocol expansion unless absolutely necessary.

key_elements.description: Existing room-chat contract that should remain the transport source of truth.

gotchas.text: Steady-state post-auth ENet ownership is not yet explicit anywhere in the current HC-105 plan and must be implemented before authoritative receive behavior is possible.
Reducer or state metadata is currently too weak for authoritative selected-server, room, and self-versus-other gating.
DM compose UI exists, but the server contract in scope is shared room chat only, so unsupported DM must fail narrowly instead of appearing successful.

security_considerations.concern: Room-chat packets must continue to use established encrypted transport helpers and authenticated session state.
Do not add DM protocol or broaden room semantics while revising HC-105.

testing_patterns.test_organization: Client-focused tests belong in client/main_test.odin and should be run with odin test client.
mock_patterns: Reuse the HC-103 test-friendly startupAuthBridge default where possible.
Prefer focused reducer or runtime seam assertions over end-to-end multi-process automation.

domain_context.error_handling: Prefer an existing narrow error surface when possible; failed or unsupported send must not look like delivered chat.
domain_context.data_flow: view callback -> reducer message -> explicit steady-state runtime owner -> encrypted transport send or receive -> structured inbound event with metadata -> authoritative reducer append -> render

open_questions.question: What is the smallest inbound event shape that can represent transport source, room identity, and self-versus-other state without widening protocol scope?
open_questions.context: Needed to convert the reducer seam from placeholder receive behavior to authoritative append behavior.

open_questions.question: Should failed send reuse an existing error surface or add one narrow chat-specific status field?
open_questions.context: Needed to provide failure-path UX without scope creep.

prior_decisions.decision: Steady-state post-auth ENet poll and dispatch ownership is a first-class HC-105 implementation slice.
rationale: The critique identifies the missing runtime owner as blocking.
Authoritative receive behavior cannot exist without a real runtime owner.
linked_constraints: HC-105 must now treat steady-state ENet poll and dispatch ownership as a first-class implementation slice.

prior_decisions.decision: Room chat echoed from the server is the visible source of truth.
rationale: Aligns the client with HC-104 server broadcast behavior.
linked_constraints: Real server-backed room chat is the source of truth for visible room history.

prior_decisions.decision: Startup auth ownership remains in client/main.odin.
rationale: HC-103 already established a selected-server startup owner.
HC-105 only needs steady-state post-auth extensions.
linked_constraints: Startup auth lifecycle remains owned by client/main.odin.
